texts.facts: 1. Vide the present commercial suit, plaintiffs seek permanent injunction restraining infringement of trademark, dilution, passing off, unfair competition, damages, rendition of accounts etc. against defendant. 2. Briefly stated, facts of the present case as averred in the plaint are that plaintiff no.1 is the proprietor of M/s EXPOSE APPARELS as well as one of the Directors of plaintiff no.2 which is a Private Limited Company incorporated under The Companies Act. Plaintiffs are engaged in the well-known and well-established business of manufacturing and marketing inter-alia of Readymade Garments, Wearing apparels, Hosiery, Under Garments, Fashion wears and Fashion accessories (hereinafter referred to as the "said goods"). 3. Plaintiff No.1 is the owner and registered proprietor of trademark "X'POSE" by virtue of application dated 08.03.1994 under No.621615 in class 25 in respect of the "said goods". The said trademark was coined and adopted by plaintiff no.1 in the year 1993 and since then has been used continuously, extensively and exclusively. The plaintiff no.2 is using the said trademark "X'POSE" of the plaintiff no.1 by way of permitted use. 4. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that the plaintiff no.1 also represents its trademark "X'POSE" in an original, Digitally signed by HEMANI CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 HEMANI MALHOTRA contd/....... 2025.03.03 15:20:37 +0530 unique and eye-catching logo which is also registered under the Provision of Copyright Act'1956. 5. It is further the case of the plaintiffs that on account of continuous use of trademark "X'POSE" plaintiffs have earned goodwill and reputation, so much so that the trademark "X'POSE" is exclusively identified with the plaintiffs. 6. Plaintiff has also incurred huge expenses to promote his product under the trademark "X'POSE" through various medium of advertisements. Thus, the expenses on advertisements grew from zero in 1995-1996 to 15.12 lacs in 2021-2022. Similarly, the sales grew from 8.91 lacs in 1995-96 to Rs.2593 lacs in 2021-2022. 7. The plaintiff No.1 also applied for and obtained registration of the trademark "EXPOSE" in respect of goods in different classes including class 25 and 35. Plaintiff no.1 also obtained copyright registration for his mark "X'POSE" in various artistic variants. The plaintiffs have been active on various social media platforms and selling its goods from various well known e- commerce platforms and the website www.xposejeans.com as well as through all leading stores contd/....... HEMANI MALHOTRA Date: 2025.03.03 15:22:14 +0530 selling readymade garments in Delhi and other parts of the country. 9. It is further averred that since it is trending now a days in the world of fashion that the worldwide leading and famous clothes and apparels brands owners are opening brand caf and restaurant near their offline stores, in which the customers after shopping for their products in the store can relax and dine in their brand caf and restaurant, the plaintiff may also launch a similar brand caf under the trademark "X'POSE" and hence the Plaintiff No.1 has duly got his trademark registered in class 43. This is also pertinent to note that the defendant has not objected nor opposed the registration of plaintiff's trademark X'POSE in Class 43. This happening trend establishes that trade and public are likely to associate a lounge or restaurant under the trademark X'POSE with the plaintiff only. 10. It is alleged that the defendant is a private limited company and it is in the business of running "Lounge and Bar" under the identical trademark/tradename "XPOSE LOUNGE" (hereinafter referred to as "the impugned trademark") from Delhi. 11. Plaintiff no.1 through his attorneys came to know that an application for registration of impugned trademark "XPOSE" in class 43 was filed with the false user claim of January'2016. The plaintiff immediately filed an Digitally CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 signed by MALHOTRA contd/....... HEMANI MALHOTRA Date: 2025.03.03 15:22:24 +0530 Opposition against the said application on 21.11.2016 to oppose the registration of impugned Trade Mark by the Defendant. The said Notice of Opposition was served to the defendant on 05/07/2017 and no counter statement was filed by Defendant to the said opposition of Plaintiff No.1. As a result, the said application of the Defendant was abandoned by the Registrar of Trade Marks by operation of section 21(2) of the Trade Mark Act,1999. Consequently, plaintiff assumed that defendant had stopped using the said trademark. However, to the plaintiff's surprise, during mid-December 2022, the Plaintiffs came across the business of the defendant bearing the impugned trademark/trade name "XPOSE LOUNGE", wherein the defendant was found to be promoting and advertising its restaurant and lounge business through various social media handles and taking reservations through various third party websites. 12. Consequently, plaintiff No.1 issued a cease and desist notice dated 11.01.2023 to which defendant sent a false reply denying the averments of plaintiff. Summons of the suit were issued to defendant and defendant who was duly served through email on 01.09.2023 and through ordinary process on 13.009.2023. However, despite service, written statement was not filed on behalf of defendant within the stipulated period of 30 CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 Resultantly, vide order dated 16.01.2024, defence was struck off and matter was listed for PE. 14. In support of their case, plaintiffs examined, Plaintiff no.1 Sh. Subodh Kumar Chachra as PW1. In this case, respondent company was manufacturing and selling various agricultural equipment, razor blades, tractors, washing machines, motorcycles, shock absorbers, thermometers and other medical appliances since 1951. In 1953, the appellant sought registration of trademark 'Escort' in respect of electric irons, electric kettles, shouldering irons and elements for electric irons and kettles. The respondents filed an opposition to the CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 Thereafter, respondent preferred appeal before the Single Bench of Hon'ble Madras High Court which was allowed. The appellant preferred an appeal against the judgment before the DB of the Madras High Court which was dismissed.
texts.arguments: 15. It was vehemently argued by learned counsel for plaintiffs that in the present case, provisions of Section 29(1) and (4) of The Trade Marks Act, 1999 were squarely attracted and the defendant had failed to rebut the claim of plaintiffs in the cross-examination of PW1. He also urged that Section 29 (1) and (4) of The Trade Marks Act'1999 (hereinafter referred to as 'The Act') are self explanatory and provide for circumstances in which infringement of registered trade marks in the present case is made out. 16. Learned counsel for plaintiffs further asserted that admittedly, plaintiffs were not using the brand "X'POSE" for class 43 but the same was registered by plaintiff no.1 on 08.07.2016 vide application number 3304406. He submitted that it is settled law that plaintiffs were not required to prove use of a trademark to claim infringement of registered trademark. He also explicitly pointed out that the application of defendant dated 12.02.2016 for registration of impugned trademark "X'POSE" in class 43 showing User Detail from 30.01.2016 was abandoned by defendant, immediately after, opposition dated 21.11.2016 to the application of defendant was filed by the plaintiffs. Hence, admittedly, the trademark "X'POSE" under class 43 was never got registered by defendant and plaintiff no.1 was the registered proprietor of trademark "X'POSE" in class 43. Learned counsel for plaintiffs further relied upon judgment titled as AMERICAN HOME PRODUCTS CORPORATION VS. MAC LABORATORIES PVT LTD AND ANR. reported as (1986)1 SCC 465. 17. Per contra, the main thrust of argument of learned counsel for defendant was that mark of plaintiff was registered for a specific class i.e. Class 25 and the plaintiffs' market and exposure was limited to apparels and like products only, which has been specifically admitted by PW1/plaintiff no.1 during his cross examination. Further, that Class 25 pertains to clothing, footwear and headgear, whereas Class 43 pertains to services for providing food, drink and temporary accommodation, which admittedly plaintiff is not indulging in. Also, as per the admission of PW1 in his cross examination, he has never used the trademark "X'POSE" for class 43 and has shown no intention to use it in future. Learned counsel for defendant thus contended that mere registration of brand under Class 43 without any usage or intention to use after expiry of five years of registration, tantamounts to abandoning the mark. He further argued that since plaintiffs and defendant are using the mark for different purposes, in different classes, thus, as per settled law that one cannot Subodh Chachra Proprietor Of M/S Expose ... vs V2 Promoters Pvt Ltd on 3 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172490115/ 5 have blanket proprietary right over any word, plaintiffs cannot have any proprietary right over the word "X'POSE". Section 29 (1) & (4) (a) of The Act postulates that : (1) A registered trade mark is infringed by a person who, not being a registered proprietor or a person using by way of permitted use, uses in the course of trade, a mark which is identical with, or deceptively similar to, the trade mark in relation to goods or services in respect of which the trade mark is registered. In the judgment titled as AMERICAN HOME PRODUCTS CORPORATION (SUPRA) relied upon by learned counsel for plaintiffs, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:- Subodh Chachra Proprietor Of M/S Expose ... vs V2 Promoters Pvt Ltd on 3 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172490115/ 6 Learned counsel for plaintiffs to further hammer this principle of law, also relied upon judgment titled as DALIP CHAND AGGARWAL AND ORS (SUPRA). 25. The judgment cited by learned counsel for defendant i.e. M/S NANDHINI DELUXE (SUPRA) also does not come to the Digitally signed by CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 HEMANI contd/....... MALHOTRA Date: 2025.03.03 15:23:26 +0530 rescue of defendant. Unlike, the facts and circumstances of the case cited by learned counsel for defendant (supra) in the present case the word "X'POSE" has neither any dictionary meaning nor it is a generic word. The plaintiff No.1 had got registered the word "X'POSE" in class 43 in the year 2016, whereas defendant had abandoned his application for registration of trademark "X'POSE" in Class 43. 26. Learned counsel for defendant also laid much stress on his argument that the plaintiffs had not intention to use the trademark "X'POSE" for services falling in Class 43 and in view of the judgment of VISHNUDAS TRADING AS VISHNUDAS VS THE VAZIR SULTAN TOBACCOCO. LTD AIR 1996 SUPREME COURT 2275, the plaintiffs cannot be permitted to enjoy monopoly in Class of goods and services falling under Class 43. In the case of VISHNUDAS TRADING, respondent was using 'Charminar' for cigarettes and appellant for quimam and zarda; both falling under Class 34 of the 4th Schedule to the Rules framed under the Trade Marks Act in 1940 and 1950. The appellant applied for registration of quimam and zarda with trademark 'Charminar' to which respondent raised objection. The Joint Registrar of Trade Mark observed that since the registration was of the trademark made in favour of the respondent in respect of "manufactured tobacco" which would also include quimam and zarda, the objection of respondent could not be waived. Appellant filed rectification application which was allowed by the Digitally CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 signed by HEMANI MALHOTRA contd/....... 27. The facts and circumstances in the case of Vishnu Das (Supra) are distinguishable from the facts of the present case simply for the reason that unlike the mark 'Charminar', "X'POSE" is an invented word which has no dictionary meaning and was coined by plaintiff No.1 way back in 1993-94. Moreover, PW1 in his testimony, nowhere deposed that plaintiff has no intention to carry on business of hospitality. 28. Similarly, the judgment of CONSOLIDATED FOODS CORPORATION VS. BRANDON AND COMPANY PRIVATE LTD. also does not support the contention of learned counsel for defendant. 29. In the judgment of INSTITUTE OF DIRECTORS VS WORLDDEVCORP TECHNOLOGY AND BUSINESS SOLUTIONS PVT LTD AND ORS (SUPRA) , also cited by learned counsel for defendant, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi dealt with application of plaintiff under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 CPC. Learned counsel for plaintiffs further urged that plaintiffs had also successfully established a case of passing off by defendant as well. In this regard, he relied upon judgments titled as HONDA MOTORS CO. LTD. VS. CHARANJIT SINGH & ORS., reported as 2002 SCC ONLINE DEL 1332; Subodh Chachra Proprietor Of M/S Expose ... vs V2 Promoters Pvt Ltd on 3 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172490115/ 10 KAMAL TRADING CO., BOMBAY ANR ORS. VS. GILLETTE U.K. LTD., MIDDLE SEX, ENGLAND, reported as 1987 SCC ONLINE BOM 754; ESSEL PACKAGING LTD. AND ORS. VS. ESSEL TEA EXPORTS LTD., reported as 1997 SCC ONLINE BOM 253 and BHAVNESH MOHANLAL AMIN VS. NIRMA CHEMICAL WORKS LTD., reported as 2005 SCC ONLINE GUJ 86. 32. In HONDA MOTORS (SUPRA) plaintiff, a well-established company with a global repute, was manufacturing and selling electronic appliances, cars, and motorcycles etc. The defendant company was manufacturing pressure CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 Defendant company also applied for registration of this trade name but the registrar rejected it. The defendant contended that his company had acquired a reputation around the world by the name of Honda. 33. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi applied the test of Goodwill in this matter and held that the act of the defendant "caused damage to the reputation of the plaintiff as the defendant's trademark "HONDA" for a pressure cooker is deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff's". Also, it creates puzzlement in the psyche of the purchasers. Hence, the court restrained the defendant from using the mark "HONDA" in respect of pressure cookers or any other allied and cognate goods or any other trademark which were identical with and deceptively similar to the trademark HONDA and to do anything which amounts to passing off their goods as the goods of the plaintiff. 34. In this judgment, the Hon'ble High Court also reiterated the settled law w.r.t. passing off action. It held as under:- "14. In a nutshell, in an action for passing off, the plaintiff has to establish that his business or goods has acquired the reputation he is claiming, by showing that, his trade name has become distinctive of his goods and the purchasing public at large associates the plaintiff's name with them. 35. In KAMAL TRADING CO. (SUPRA), the respondent had been using the trademark 7 o'clock since 1913 for manufacture and sale of safety razor blades, safety razors, shaving Digitally signed by CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 HEMANI contd/....... In the challenge before the Hon'ble High Court of Bombay, the appeal was dismissed and it was held that the trademark 7 O'clock had acquired worldwide reputation and any customer purchasing the goods with that mark would immediately connect the goods to the house of Gillette which are registered owner of the registered mark 7 O'clock. The Hon'ble Bombay High Court also opined that it cannot overlook that it is not necessary for plaintiffs (respondent) to establish that in fact any customer was deceived but it is enough if it is shown that there is likelihood of deception. 36. Similarly, in ESSEL PACKAGING LTD. & ORS. (SUPRA), the Hon'ble Bombay High Court restrained use of trademark "essel" for tea in a passing off action brought by the prior user and reputation of trade name "essel" in respect of packaging materials and amusement parks. In Subodh Chachra Proprietor Of M/S Expose ... vs V2 Promoters Pvt Ltd on 3 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172490115/ 12 Bhavnesh Mohanlal Amin (supra), the Hon'ble Gujarat High Court restrained use of trademark "NIMA" for floor mills (ghar ghanti) on the suit for passing off filed by prior owners/ users of trademark NIRMA/NIMA used for detergents, soaps, spices, matchbox etc. 37. As stated above, the plaintiffs by virtue of invoices (Ex. Digit signe CS (COMM.) NO.561/2023 HEMAN contd/....... MALHOTRA D 2025. 15:24 +0530 PW1/7 (colly.) and Ex. PW1/8 (invoices) and copies of advertisement and photographs of advertisement (Ex. PW1/9, Ex. PW1/10 and Ex. PW1/11 colly.) firmly established that plaintiffs trademark "X"POSE had acquired goodwill and reputation among the public and trade during the past 30 years of their existence and that their trade name "X'POSE" had become distinctive. Further, that defendant's use of trade name "X'POSE" even if, for distinctive goods is likely to cause confusion/deception in the minds of public at large. Thus, proving an action of passing off. PUNITIVE DAMAGES: 38. It is the case of plaintiffs that they have suffered and are likely to suffer irreparable loss and injury to their goodwill and reputation on account of aforesaid acts of unfair trade practice committed by the defendants. In the instant matter, the plaintiffs have sought both reliefs i.e. rendition of accounts and damages which on plain reading of Section Subodh Chachra Proprietor Of M/S Expose ... vs V2 Promoters Pvt Ltd on 3 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172490115/ 13 135(1) of The Trademarks Act cannot together be granted. It was the argument of learned counsel for plaintiffs that the plaintiffs be awarded Punitive Damages which have been assessed/ estimated as Rs. 20,00,000/-. In this regard, learned counsel for plaintiffs cited judgments titled as MICROSOFT CORPORATION VS RAJENDRA PAWAR & ANR 2008 (36)PTC 698 (DEL.) and MOTORLA INC & ANR. VS. MOTORLA AUTO INDIA PVT LTD & ORS 2015 (64) PTC 600 (DEL). 41. In a recent judgment titled as CALVIN KLEIN TRADEMARK TRUST & ANR Vs. M/S GURU NANAK INTERNATIONAL & ORS. decided on 08.12.2023, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi opined as under:- "28. On the issue of damages, the settled legal position has been laid down in Hindustan Unilever Limited v. Reckitt Benckiser India Ltd. (2014) 57 PTC 495 (DB), by the ld. Division Bench. In the said decision, the ld. Division Bench has clearly held that unless there are extenuating circumstances and overwhelming evidence of wrong doing, punitive damages cannot be awarded.

On the issue of damages, the settled legal position has been laid down in Hindustan Unilever Limited v. Reckitt Benckiser India Ltd. (2014) 57 PTC 495 (DB), by the ld. Division Bench.
